name: the Parc de la Ciutadella
title: Ancient Trees in the Parc de la Ciutadella, Barcelona: 7 to Find
meta_description: Barcelona's first public park, laid over a demolished fortress for the 1888 exposition. Seven remarkable trees, most planted within fifteen years.
intro: This park is a fortress the city pulled down. The citadel that gave it its name was built to hold Barcelona after 1714, demolished in the 1870s, and the ground rebuilt as the city's first public park for the Universal Exposition of 1888, which is why almost everything old here dates from one fifteen year window. A Mexican white oak went in around 1887 and is the only one of its kind alive in Catalonia. A river she-oak followed beside the Cascada around 1894, its drooping grey green needles actually jointed twigs. A silk tree has flowered every July since about 1896, well past the age its species normally reaches. The stoutest black locust in Barcelona is here, 4.3 metres around on twelve metres of tree, and so is a plane nobody has ever cut back to knuckles, which is simply what the species does when left alone.
